fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. "…Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines…" while he was still alive, and then he sent them away from his son Isaac to the land of the east (Genesis 25:6). Gifts is the word the verse uses. The text doesn't say what the gifts were, so I won't guess.

Good guess, friend, since Terah was Abraham's father (Genesis 11:27). But he isn't named in this verse. It says Abraham "was buried there with his wife Sarah." (Genesis 25:10). That's the name the text gives us.

Nahor was Abraham's brother (Genesis 11:27), so I see why he popped into your head, friend. But he's not the one in this verse. The text says Abraham was buried in the field he bought from the Hittites, "…with his wife Sarah." (Genesis 25:10).

Yes, baker! "After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac…" (Genesis 25:11). Abraham was gone, but God's blessing was still going. The verse says Isaac lived near Beer-lahai-roi. Blessed is the word the text gives, and I'm happy to leave it right there.

Close to a real moment, friend, because God did test Abraham earlier, when He told him to offer up Isaac (Genesis 22:1-2). But this verse is different. It says God "blessed" Isaac after Abraham died (Genesis 25:11). Blessing, not testing, this time.

Milcah is a name from Abraham's family, friend. She was the wife of his brother Nahor (Genesis 11:27, 29). She isn't Ishmael's mother, though. The verse says he was born to "…Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s maidservant…" (Genesis 25:12).

That's right, baker. Genesis 25:18 says Ishmael's descendants "…lived in hostility toward all their brothers." Not peace, hostility. I think that's a heavy note to end on. The text doesn't say more about why.
